subject: Post-call: technical validation & 1M-token cost delta (EdgeFin trial plan)
messages:
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: Hannah Cho <hannah@edgefin.com>, Tom Barnes <tom.barnes@edgefin.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 7 Dec 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: technical validation & 1M-token cost delta (EdgeFin trial plan)

Hannah / Tom — thanks again for the call this afternoon. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Key takeaways from discovery:
- Workload: multi-turn chat assistant for customer support; avg prompt ~350 tokens, avg reply ~60 tokens; peak QPS target ~20 sustained with spikes to ~60.
- Important SLOs: 95th p90 latency target ~300ms for short chats, p95 targets for long context (up to 1k tokens) ~800ms.
- Main buyer concerns: per-1M token economics, predictable unit cost as usage scales, and ability to hit high cache hit rates for repeated dialogues.
- Competitive comparisons: EdgeFin is benchmarking against their hyperscaler contracts (AWS Bedrock / GCP Vertex) and a small self-hosted setup.

What we propose Redwood validate next:
1) Cost model delta: run a short simulation that outputs per-1M token cost under three configs — (A) Hosted API (standard caching), (B) Hosted + 50% KV prefix cache hit, (C) Dedicated reserved capacity (monthly commit).
2) Latency sweep: bench batching sizes {1,4,8} across expected sequence lengths (prompt 350 + completion 60, and a 1k token scenario). Provide p50/p90/p95 numbers.
3) Cache sensitivity: simulate 30% / 50% / 70% KV cache hit scenarios and show token savings and effective cost per 1M tokens.

Attachments: edgefin-requirements-summary.pdf (the doc you shared), baseline-cost-params.csv (our input assumptions).

Ask / next steps:
- Marcus, can your team run the sim & latency sweep and drop initial numbers by EOD Wednesday (12/09)? Please include the raw sim CSV and the scenario configs.
- Ben / Marissa, I'll coordinate pricing and a draft mutual action plan for procurement. Hannah — could you confirm procurement timeline and any constraints (e.g., PO lead times, legal items)?

Hannah — we want to make the comparison apples-to-apples. We'll report both list-rate comparisons and a committed-VM projection for Dedicated so you can see a likely floor on unit cost.

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni | Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 09:40:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Post-call: technical validation & 1M-token cost delta (EdgeFin trial plan)

Quick technical readout and proposed test plan — initial back-of-envelope numbers included.

Assumptions used for the quick model:
- Model: redwood-large-v2 (approx cost baseline)
- Input/completion mix: 350-token prompt + 60-token completion average
- Tokenization and overhead: +10% pad for prompt framing & metadata

Back-of-envelope per-1M token comparison (list-rate style):
- Hyperscaler (bedrock/vertex estimated blended): ~$160 / 1M tokens (no caching, list)
- Redwood Hosted (no caching): ~$120 / 1M tokens
- Redwood Hosted + KV cache @50% hit: ~$72 / 1M tokens (effective tokens billed ~50%)
- Redwood Dedicated (committed 3-month): ~$48-$65 / 1M tokens depending on commit size + batching optimization

Notes: these figures include basic batching at size 4 and standard fp16 execution; quantized paths and larger batching can reduce the Dedicated floor further. They are intentionally conservative — we assume 40% model serving overhead for short-turn traffic.

Planned tests (I will run these and drop CSVs):
- Throughput/lats: run a replay for 100k requests with sequence lengths: short (350+60) and long (1k+200) and batching {1,4,8}. Collect p50/p90/p95 and failure rate.
- Cache sweep: replay same workload with synthetic cache-hit toggles at 30/50/70% and report token billable delta.
- Cost model: produce a single CSV that maps billable tokens -> cost under our hosted and dedicated offerings, and a separate sheet for the hyperscaler blended estimate.

Attachments: sim-config.json (test harness config, includes batch sizes and sequence distributions). I'll also drop raw sim CSVs as 1m-token-batch-sim.csv when tests complete.

Timeline: start runs today, initial CSVs by EOD Wednesday (12/09), final summarized deck by Friday (12/11).

-Marcus
Marcus Lin | Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Vivek
